title: Workload Echo Profiler and Conservative Batch Applier
creator: Priya Raman
description: Build a conservative recommendation engine that profiles live request signatures (the 'echo') to synthesize conservative batching and KV-cache parameters. The goal is to produce safe, incremental configuration patches that reduce per-token cost while preserving latency SLOs and avoiding tail-regression for high-priority customers.
acceptance_criteria: Profiler generates 24h workload signature summary with per-route percentiles (p50/p95/p99) and request shape histograms
Heuristic engine emits a ranked list of batching/caching parameter suggestions with estimated cost delta and risk score
Apply workflow can push conservative patches via the 'conservative' channel in Console with automatic shadow-apply and canary rollout settings
Automatic rollback criteria trigger when p95 latency increases by >10% or error-rate increases by >0.5% for the target cohort
End-to-end e2e test and staging rollout validated on dev-dedicated with synthetic microburst traces
updates: 2026-02-18: Kickoff - scoped to box: route-level profiling, heuristic scorer, safe-apply pipeline. Priya and Liam aligned on minimal viable outputs.
2026-02-24: Probe design doc posted to Confluence (see links). Chose lightweight sketching for request signatures to keep telemetry low-cost.

2026-03-02: Initial profiler implemented (daemon) and deployed to shadow collector for 50% of traffic on staging. Captures prefix lengths, sequence length distribution, KV hit ratios, and arrival delta histograms.
2026-03-06: Heuristic prototype scoring: combines cost-gain estimate, latency-sensitivity signal, and tail-risk penalty. Tuned parameters after running on 72h of replay data.
2026-03-09: Safety policy drafted: conservative amplitude caps, minimum TTL for cache suggestions, and rollout throttles. Security review requested; no customer data persisted beyond 7 days.
2026-03-12: Shadow apply completed for two internal routes; observed 6% token-cost reduction with <1% p95 change. Preparing canary plan for broader pilot next week.
implementation_notes: Profiler runs as a lightweight sidecar-less collector to avoid per-request tail impact; uses reservoir sampling for rare shapes.
Heuristic scoring favors cache TTL increases and microbatch size increases only when KV-hit probability > threshold and tail-risk < threshold.

Safe apply flow: generate JSON patch -> dry-run in shadow mode -> metric-checker compares baseline vs treatment -> if within thresholds, promote to canary with gradual traffic ramping -> full apply after 72h stable.
Rollback plan: immediate circuit-breaker if canary triggers alarms. Rollback script reverts to previous config and issues incident ticket automatically.
Telemetry: add cost-estimate, p50/p95/p99, error-rate, kv-hit-rate per suggestion; store for 30 days for trend analysis.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-aggressive batching could increase p99 latency for spiky routes. Mitigation: risk penalty in scorer and hard cap on batch growth per apply.
Risk: Telemetry overhead adds noise. Mitigation: sketching and sampling with per-tenant budgets.
Risk: Misclassification of customer-sensitive traffic. Mitigation: opt-out list and explicit allowlist for pilot customers.
